items.title: Bobby Militello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002
items.q: I get to go out on the road, on a bus, and hang out with Conte Candoli, Snooky Young, you know, all the cats.

ctx.x: So I walk into the original quartet, which is like a dream, I mean I had memorized all those Desmond things and all that stuff. So I walked in and had done my homework on the new tunes. But I didn’t have to do my homework on the old tunes because I already knew them. So Dave says, “Well what do you want to play?” I said, “Anything you want. Anything you want to play.” And he tells this in his interviews now to people. So he says, “Play some of the new tunes” and I played them right out. That’s cool. And then they…

sudden he falls in love. Now the next time he comes back to Buffalo there’s four saxophone solos that he’s put in there because he knows I’m here. And he’s asking for me. Now he takes me out to do a couple of other orchestra dates with him, in other cities, and then asked me if I wanted to do the Tonight Show band when they take it on the road. I said yeah, hell yes. And I get to go out on the road, on a bus, and hang out with Conte Candoli, Snooky Young, you know, all the cats. The real deal. I mean these cats…
